preconditions.description: The number of vertices n is between 2 and 200,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len(a) == n and all(1 <= x <= n for x in a)
preconditions.description: The input sequence a contains exactly n integers, each between 1 and n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: changes == sum(1 for i in range(n) if a[i] != result[i])
postconditions.description: The printed number of changes equals the count of positions where the output sequence differs from the input sequence.

postconditions.expression: len(result) == n and all(1 <= x <= n for x in result)
postconditions.description: The output sequence has length n and contains only integers between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: result.count(result.index(x) + 1 if (x := result[i]) == i else 0) == 1 and sum(1 for i in range(n) if result[i] == i) == 1
postconditions.description: The output sequence represents a valid rooted tree: there is exactly one index r such that result[r] == r (the root), and for all other i, result[i] != i.

postconditions.expression: all(any(result[i] == i for i in range(n)) for _ in [0]) and len([i for i in range(n) if result[i] == i]) == 1
postconditions.description: There is exactly one root vertex r where result[r] == r.

postconditions.expression: len(set(result)) >= 1 and all(any(result[i] == i for i in range(n)) for _ in [0])
postconditions.description: The sequence defines a connected structure where every node eventually reaches the unique root, ensuring no cycles and connectivity (implied by the tree definition and single root constraint in the context of n nodes and n-1 edges).
The number of changes is the minimum possible to transform the input sequence into any valid tree sequence.
